purpose: Kortkoncept med terræn knyttet til skills og kamphabitater
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create the FULL GAME MAP concept for TalenttreeIncremental, in the exact hand-inked fantasy COMIC style of the reference, but now with STRONGLY DIFFERENTIATED TERRAIN tied to each skill and each combat encounter.
Input image: visual style and UI vocabulary reference only. It is a moodboard. The new image must be one single coherent playable-looking world map occupying the entire landscape canvas, no moodboard sidebar, no asset samples, no palette swatches, no giant title.

Format: landscape 3:2, high resolution around 2400x1600 or the nearest supported size. Flat screen-facing illustrated world map viewed from a consistent high oblique cartographic angle; UI cards remain flat front-facing. Thick lively near-black ink contours, flat rich colour areas, two or three cel-shaded tones, warm cream highlights, restrained hatching and printed paper texture. Match the reference's oak tree, copper breastplate and expressive goblin. No photorealism or glossy 3D.

PRIMARY DESIGN OBJECTIVE:
Territory must communicate the activity even if every label is hidden. Actual landcover, ground shapes, geological formations and vegetation must differ, not just differently coloured frames. Avoid a uniform beige parchment ground across the entire map. Parchment is used for card labels and narrow paths; the world itself has strongly readable green, blue-grey, charcoal, ochre and violet terrain masses. Keep the terrain calmer immediately behind UI cards so the game remains readable. About 55 percent of the canvas remains visible terrain. Natural boundaries through ridges, riverbanks, forest edges and elevation changes; not boxed panels or a collage of rectangular biomes. One river and branching footpaths create a connected place.

REGIONS / COMPOSITION:
UPPER LEFT, "TRÆFÆLDNING": a lush sunlit deciduous forest. Rounded lime and deep-green oak crowns, lighter birch grove, willow trees along a blue riverbank, grassy soil, visible stumps and a small timber clearing. Three modest cards for Eg, Birk and Pil plus one small axe modifier; green hand-inked connectors.
UPPER MIDDLE, "MINEDRIFT": a sharply distinct terraced blue-grey rocky quarry in a craggy ridge, almost no trees, dusty gravel, exposed orange copper bands low on the cliff and silver-blue iron seams higher up, mine entrance and short rail track. Two cards for Kobbermalm and Jernmalm plus a pickaxe modifier; blue connectors. The forest gives way to exposed bedrock along the ridge.
UPPER RIGHT, "SMEDJE": a small forge yard on charcoal-black cobblestones, rust-red clinker and ash, brick furnace, anvil, stacks of billets, restrained ember-orange light. This is a medieval work yard, not a volcano. A copper breastplate card, sword card and furnace card; warm orange connectors. Access road leads from the mine.
MIDDLE RIGHT, "HJEMMEBASE": sheltered warm ochre meadow with a cottage, vegetable plots, low fences and an orderly woodpile; calm cream and golden palette. A cottage card and one small building socket. A bridge links this meadow with the other regions.

COMBAT IS A ROUTE THROUGH SEVERAL DISTINCT HABITATS, NOT ONE RED PATCH:
Across the middle-left/lower-middle under a modest red "KAMP" banner, follow a red route from LEFT to RIGHT:
1. "Rotte": a damp shaded stream culvert and muddy bank with reeds and small burrow holes; rat portrait card.
2. "Goblin": a trampled brown-earth camp at the edge of the woods with rough wooden palisades and patched leather shelters; expressive goblin portrait card.
3. "Ulv": a colder, desaturated pine forest ridge with slate boulders, sparse grass and wolf tracks; silver-grey wolf portrait card.
Each of these three combat cards must visibly sit inside its own habitat. Small consistent portrait frames and HP strips, no crowded stat tables. The connecting path crosses natural terrain transitions.

LOWER RIGHT, "DEN HULE EG": an ominous ancient overgrown wood, a colossal hollow oak as the landmark, exposed tangled roots, moss-covered stones, damp dark earth and muted wine-red details. A tiny bark beetle encounter card and a larger tree-guardian boss card near the hollow; the guardian is made of bark and branches, NOT a rock golem. Keep the hollow itself visible.
LOWER LEFT, "DRUIDE": a small mystical violet-green woodland glade with softly lit herbs, mossy standing stones and a moon motif, violet plant accents, two modest herb/root skill cards. Organic natural glade, not a mushroom-only biome.
LOWER CENTRE, "SKOVBRUG": an adjacent teal-green managed woodland with neat nursery rows, saplings, fresh shoots sprouting beside harvested stumps, two small planting/sustainable-felling cards. Visually distinguish orderly new growth from the dense old forest.

UI:
Preserve the reference's hand-inked node frames, cream label strips, small angular skill banners and tidy curved coloured connectors. About 20-23 cards total, no giant cards covering the landscapes. One small family banner per region, subordinate to the map. Only use the quoted Danish region titles and short node labels; minimal other text and no decorative statistics. Distinct activity and combat silhouettes, consistent outlines. Leave breathing space around all banners and cards. At the very outer lower corners a little torn parchment/fog may hint at more unexplored land with only two small dashed question-mark nodes. No test-asset column and no explanatory text.

The result should look like a cohesive, inviting, readable game map where geography explains progression and each skill has a recognizable place.
